reviewText: Megaton brings a cheese-grater approach to the editing of the action scenes, flitting from one angle to the next with no apparent concern for the effectiveness of any of them.
The original Taken was a much better movie than anyone thought it would be. Taken 3, on the other hand, is the movie everyone did think Taken was going to be.
Taken 3 makes clear that the only place left for this franchise to be taken is out back, and put out of its misery.
"Taken 3″ is easily the weakest of the three films. Oh, sure, Neeson kicks some backside. But, this time the plotting is feeble and the action scenes are just barely acceptable.
This is a movie as its own death wish. To call it cheap, lazy, and perfunctory grants it a dignity that implies there was another path it could have taken.
Ant-Man and The Wasp: Quantumania takes you on a fun adventure. And, as always, stay back for Easter eggs in the mid and post credit scenes.
Taken 3 ends as it began -- another segment in a bloated, lazily drawn cash cow that offers a few laughs and high octane chases.
One of Marvel's most visually inventive films with fantastical world-building, and the franchise's most imposing villain yet in Kang the Conqueror.
... "Quantumania" is a stellar time. ... some truly trippy sequences, some genuine excitement, and the characteristic laughs the "Ant-Man" films offer, and "Quantumania" is a strong start to Phase 5.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania is an epic sci-fi adventure that explores the family dynamics against the backdrop of a sci-fi war movie.
The kind of thing you give to Gary Busey, not the Oscar-nominated star of 'The Grey' (a masterpiece).

Despite being an example of why a movie shouldn’t be shot almost entirely in The Volume, every time Jonathan Majors steps on screen as Kang, Ant-Man and The Wasp: Quantumania is an epic tale to astonish and a monumental chapter in the Multiverse Saga.
If the tagline It Ends Here is true then it's a poor finale, but perhaps it's the right time it is taken off our screens.
[Peyton Reed] does an adequate job mixing the wacky silliness of [Jeff] Loveness’ script with a surprisingly hefty amount of a dark and serious tone this time around.

A perfectly enjoyable, perfectly disposable post-content popcorn seller...essentially an animated film where the cast performed most of their roles in front of green screens... a good film to chew gum to.
Naturally, the special effects in Peyton Reed’s film are dazzling. But there is such a thing as too much dazzle, for which the best-known antidote is to shut your eyes.

It takes an impressive amount of ineptitude to plonk seasoned pros such as Douglas, Pfeiffer and Murray around a table and produce little more than awkward groans as Murray wheels out his “wacky lothario” schtick.
Where the film falters, Jonathan Majors is there to lift it up with a genuinely fantastic performance as Kang. The next great Marvel villain has arrived, and somehow surpasses the hype.
Despite a smattering of jokes, Peyton Reed’s film just isn’t as much fun as the others.
A dire and crummy movie, one of the worst ever produced by Marvel.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania is an unwieldy and monotonous repackaging of what came before.
What works greatly to the movie's credit is the pacing (never a dull moment here!) and that sense of 'What's going to happen next?'
'Taken 3' scores over its predecessor on almost every level: the stakes are higher, the LA locations are nicely photographed and, best of all, there's an actual plot, with twists and everything.
Liam Neeson nails action like few others.
